title: Nasi Goreng
subtitle: Indonesian fried rice with shrimp paste and kecap manis
excerpt: Indonesia's great fried rice: day-old jasmine rice stir-fried over very high heat with shrimp paste, sweet soy sauce, chilli, and garlic until each grain is separate and slightly caramelised. Topped with a crisp fried egg and prawn crackers.

recipe.sourceNotes: Nasi goreng (fried rice in Indonesian and Malay) is the national dish of Indonesia and one of the defining dishes of Southeast Asian cooking. Every household has its own version, but the common thread is the use of kecap manis (sweet soy sauce), which gives the rice its characteristic dark caramel colour and sweet-savoury flavour, and terasi (shrimp paste), which provides its distinctive pungency. Like all good fried rice, it requires day-old cold rice: freshly cooked rice is too moist and clumps in the pan. The heat must be very high and the cook must work fast. Nasi goreng is always topped with a fried egg cooked in a little oil until the whites are just set but the yolk is still liquid, and is commonly served with krupuk (prawn crackers) and a cucumber and tomato salad.

content.text: Day-old rice is not optional: freshly cooked rice is too wet and clumps into a paste when fried. The rice must be cold and the grains must be separate. Get the wok or pan screaming hot before anything goes in; the whole cook takes only 3 to 4 minutes and everything moves fast.

items.preparation: cooked the day before; refrigerated; grains broken apart
2 for frying to top; 1 beaten and scrambled into the rice
finely sliced; deseeded for less heat

content.text: Heat a wok or large frying pan over the highest heat until smoking. Add 3 tablespoons of oil. Add the shrimp paste and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the shallots, garlic, and chilli. Stir-fry for 1 minute.

Add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps. Stir-fry vigorously over high heat for 2 minutes until each grain is separate and beginning to colour. Push the rice to the side, add the beaten egg to the centre and scramble briefly, then mix into the rice. Add the kecap manis and soy sauce and toss to coat.

Divide between two plates. In the same wok with the remaining oil, fry the eggs over high heat until the whites are set and edges are crisp but the yolk is still liquid. Place one egg on each plate of rice. Scatter with spring onions and serve with sliced cucumber.
